messages:
alex.m: quick q — we're getting requests from infra about adding per-tenant retention controls for OTEL spans. thinking: allow customers to set retention window (7d/30d/90d) at tenant config and have SDK/exporter tag spans so ingest can route/expire. any red flags?
priya.k: high-level sounds fine. main risk is buffering in SDKs: if we hold per-tenant buffers to enforce retention metadata before sending, memory spikes will be nasty. prefer adding metadata and letting collector/enricher handle retention. :thinking_face:
josh.s: agree w/ Priya. also fanout: current exporter fans out per-tenant to multiple ingest endpoints. if we add retention config in SDK, that's a lot of handshake churn when tenants change. better to push tenant-id + retention_hint header and let proxy decide.
emily.r: from runtime side, Python SDK already attaches resource.attributes['redwood.tenant_id'], but retention_hint would be new. question: how do we surface changes quickly? tenants flip retention during canary rollouts.
dan.p: console UX requirement: when support flips retention for a tenant, they expect telemetry to reflect new policy within 30s. can we make that soft real-time without hot restarts?
olga.s: SREs: we can't rely on 30s for config propagation through SDK env vars. preferred path: control plane updates a centralized config service + edge proxy polls/streams changes. SDK just sends tenant_id + retention_hint from the local cache that updates via SSE.
alex.m: implementation proposals: (A) SDK-level cache + SSE subscription to config service; add `redwood.retention` resource attr and header `x-redwood-retention`. (B) Keep SDK dumb, only send tenant_id; collector enriches with retention based on control-plane mapping.
priya.k: tradeoffs: A gives faster local correctness and less impl work on collector, but forces us to ship SSE + reconfig in all SDKs (py/go/rust). B centralizes complexity but increases collector CPU/memory and coupling.
josh.s: also consider exporter shutdown semantics: if SDK buffers until collector ack, we need graceful drain during process exit across languages. We already had bugs in Rust where drain timed out and spans lost.
emily.r: sample code idea for minimal change (B):
```
# python init snippet (minimal)
from opentelemetry import trace
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)
# attach tenant as resource attr only
# leave retention to collector/enricher
```
this avoids SSE in SDKs.
dan.p: for rollout UX, we can canary retention changes by tenant tag + ingest-side feature flag. console would show per-tenant telemetry retention state and a toggle. ops flow: flip flag -> collector routes retention -> confirm metrics -> roll.
olga.s: require telemetry metrics for transition: exporter_latency, enrichment_latency, retention_mismatch_rate (span retention header != control-plane expected). Also add an alert if retention_mismatch_rate > 0.1% after rollout.
alex.m: what about sampling? if we sample out spans before we attach tenant (rare but possible in gateway), retention decisions could be lost. Need to ensure tenant_id set as early as possible in request path.
priya.k: yes ensure instrumentations set `resource.service.instance.id` and `redwood.tenant_id` at entry. for frameworks we have middleware already. we should add test vectors for each language to guarantee ordering.
josh.s: language specifics: Go exporter uses batching with channels — adding header per-span is cheap. Rust exporter uses intrusive linked lists for batches; we must avoid per-span heap allocs when adding retention hint. So prefer resource-level attr or exporter-level header from the batch metadata rather than mutating each span.
emily.r: note for Python's async batch exporter (otlp): adding per-tenant metadata as `Resource` means we need per-tenant exporter instances to avoid mixing resources, which increases file descriptors and TCP connections. collector-side enrichment avoids that.
dan.p: decision path proposal: 1) opt for B (collector enrichment) as default to minimize SDK churn; 2) implement SSE config path as opt-in for large customers who need <30s propagation; 3) add console UX and metrics + rollout canary plan.
olga.s: +1 but add strict drain tests prior to rollout. define drain SLOs: SDKs must drain buffered spans within 5s on SIGTERM for our standard image. if any lang fails, block rollout.
alex.m: sounds good. next steps: Priya/Josh to draft SDK minimal change PR (resource attr only) and collector enrichment PR. Emily/Dan to spec console + metrics + canary steps. I'll own the rollout checklist and drain test harness.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://redwood.internal/tasks/RETENTION-EXPORTER-ROLLOUT-2418
priya.k: I'll start a small PoC in Go that keeps SDK unchanged but adds `x-redwood-retention` in the batch meta header from collector. tag me on the PR.
josh.s: I'll add drain unit tests for Rust exporter (simulate SIGTERM + backlog). will post results here.
emily.r: will prototype console toggle mock and wire up retention_mismatch_rate dashboard.
alex.m: thanks all — re-check in 24h with PoC links. :white_check_mark:
